summary: Switches the release workflow from token-based npm publishing to npm OIDC trusted publishing. It removes NPM_TOKEN from the changesets step, upgrades npm globally to a floating ^11.5.1 range, and corrects or adds `repository` metadata (url + directory) on nine published packages so they match cipherstash/stack. Library code is unchanged. The risk is in the release pipeline. With the token fallback gone, publishing depends entirely on npmjs.com-side Trusted Publisher registration for all ten publishable packages (including the unscoped `stash` CLI). None of that registration is visible here, and the repo's own supply-chain skill lists it as deferred, pending npm org admin action. If some packages are registered and others are not, a partial release could ship packages whose pinned internal dependency versions were never published. The new floating npm install also runs inside the id-token: write job without the repo's 7-day release-age cooldown. Nothing in CI can exercise the publish path before merge. The first real verification is the next release on main. SECURITY.md still describes NPM_TOKEN publishing (doc drift, low impact).

behaviour_changes.description: Publish authentication changes from the NPM_TOKEN secret (plus OIDC) to OIDC trusted publishing only. The changesets/action step no longer receives NPM_TOKEN, so it writes no token .npmrc and there is no token fallback if OIDC is rejected.

The release job now runs `npm install -g npm@^11.5.1` before `pnpm install`. This replaces Node 22's bundled npm 10.x with whatever npm 11.x is latest at run time, inside a job that holds id-token: write.

Published package metadata changes. Seven packages' repository.url/bugs.url move from cipherstash/protectjs to cipherstash/stack with a `directory`. cli, migrate and wizard gain a repository field. npm trusted publishing and provenance check repository.url against the publishing repo.

failure_scenarios.title: Missing Trusted Publisher registration for some packages produces a partial, dependency-skewed release
failure_scenarios.trigger: The next merge to main with pending changesets, when npmjs.com has no Trusted Publisher configured for cipherstash/stack + release.yml on one or more of the ten publishable packages (the unscoped `stash`, recently added migrate/wizard/prisma-next, or legacy protectjs-era packages).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: NPM_TOKEN is removed (release.yml:63-68 head), so every package must authenticate through OIDC. The in-repo skill says registration of each package is npm-org-admin work 'tracked separately' and deferred (SKILL.md:110-117). changeset publish runs per package, so registered packages publish and unregistered ones fail (E404/ENEEDAUTH). Sibling dependencies declared as workspace:* are rewritten to concrete versions at publish time.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Some new versions are on npm and others are not. For example, a new `stash` or `@cipherstash/drizzle` can depend on a `@cipherstash/stack`/`@cipherstash/protect` version that does not exist, and installs fail for every consumer until a follow-up release run publishes the rest. Published versions cannot be withdrawn after 72h. If no package is registered, the release fails closed and nothing ships.
missing_verification: Confirmation (screenshot/list from npm org settings) that every one of the ten publishable package names has a Trusted Publisher for cipherstash/stack, workflow release.yml
A dry run or a canary/snapshot publish through OIDC before relying on it for a real version bump
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Before merging, verify Trusted Publisher registration for all ten packages, including `stash`. Merge when no unrelated changesets are pending, or publish a low-risk patch first. Keep the NPM_TOKEN secret available, unused, so it can be restored quickly, and write down the rerun procedure (re-running changeset publish publishes only the missing versions).

failure_scenarios.title: Floating npm@^11.5.1 install runs unvetted code inside the id-token: write publish job
failure_scenarios.trigger: A new npm 11.x release, malicious (account/registry compromise) or simply broken, appears before or during a release run.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: release.yml:51-52 (head) installs npm by caret range at run time, with no lockfile, integrity pin or release-age cooldown. The repo's 7-day minimumReleaseAge (pnpm-workspace.yaml:21) applies to pnpm only, not to `npm install -g`. That npm then performs the OIDC token exchange and publish for every package. The existing unpinned `npm install -g node-gyp` (base and head line 47) already has the same exposure, so this widens an existing pattern rather than creating a new class.
failure_scenarios.consequence: A compromised npm build could mint publish tokens and push tampered versions of CipherStash encryption packages with valid provenance. A broken one blocks releases (loud).

existing_verification.description: tests-supply-chain.yml lints release.yml only for disabled caching; it does not check version pinning of global installs.

missing_verification: A lint rule or review check requiring exact versions for global tool installs in release.yml
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Pin an exact npm version (e.g. npm@11.x.y) that is at least as old as the repo's cooldown, or use a Node version that bundles npm >= 11.5.1. Do the same for node-gyp, and extend lint-no-workflow-caching (or a sibling lint) to reject floating global installs in release.yml.

failure_scenarios.title: OIDC path not taken by the actual publisher, so every publish fails closed
failure_scenarios.trigger: changeset publish in a pnpm workspace invokes `pnpm publish`, which might not delegate to the upgraded npm 11 or might not perform the OIDC exchange, or the upgraded npm might not be first on PATH after setup-node.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The head comment (release.yml:49-50) asserts `changeset publish` shells out to the upgraded npm. That depends on @changesets/cli 2.31.0 and pnpm 10.33.2 internals (package.json:52,66), which cannot be checked offline (no node_modules, no network).
failure_scenarios.consequence: The release job fails with auth errors after the version PR merges. No packages ship until the workflow is fixed or NPM_TOKEN is restored. Recoverable, no consumer impact.
missing_verification: Evidence from a branch/workflow_dispatch dry run that the publish step authenticates via OIDC
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Run a dry-run or canary publish from the workflow before the next real release, and watch the first release run.

verification_gaps.description: Trusted Publisher registration on npmjs.com is not visible and cannot be tested in CI, and the repo's own doc lists it as deferred.
No pre-merge exercise of the OIDC publish path (no dry run, no CI results supplied).
No check enforces exact versions for globally installed tools in the credential-bearing workflow.

recommended_controls.description: Have an npm org admin confirm Trusted Publisher entries (repo cipherstash/stack, workflow release.yml) exist for all ten publishable packages, including unscoped `stash`, before merge.
Make the first OIDC release a deliberate, small one (or a snapshot/canary tag), and watch the run.
Keep the NPM_TOKEN secret in place, unused, until a full OIDC release succeeds. Document that re-running changeset publish publishes only the missing versions if a partial release occurs.
Pin npm (and node-gyp) to exact, cooldown-aged versions in release.yml, and add a lint that rejects floating global installs.
Update SECURITY.md:140-141 and skills/stash-supply-chain-security/SKILL.md 'Deferred' section so they reflect OIDC-only publishing.

evidence.claim: The release workflow already grants id-token: write for OIDC.
NPM_TOKEN removed from the changesets/action env. Only GITHUB_TOKEN remains. publish runs `pnpm run release`.
New step installs npm@^11.5.1 globally by floating caret range.
repository.url changed from cipherstash/protectjs to cipherstash/stack with a directory. The same pattern applies across nine package.json files (changes.diff).
stash depends on @cipherstash/migrate and @cipherstash/stack via workspace:*. drizzle and protect-dynamodb likewise depend on protect/schema via workspace:*.
release script is `pnpm run build && changeset publish`, publishing all non-private workspace packages (ten under packages/ have publishConfig access public, bench is private).
The supply-chain workflow only checks that caching is disabled in release.yml. No publish-auth or pinning checks.
SECURITY.md still says release.yml publishes using OIDC and an NPM_TOKEN.
OIDC trusted publishing is listed as deferred and requires an npm org admin to register each package as a Trusted Publisher before NPM_TOKEN can be dropped.
The repo enforces a 7-day minimumReleaseAge for pnpm-resolved deps, which does not apply to `npm install -g`.
packageManager is pnpm@10.33.2. Whether its publish path uses the upgraded npm's OIDC flow was not verified.
